display.title: The Moon and the Jewish Month: Why the Moon Changes Its Shape
display.summary_short: Why the moon seems to grow and shrink each month, how the new moon was announced with mountaintop torches, and the calendar that tells us when Rosh Chodesh comes.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given in the middle of Adar Rishon. Uncle Yossi invites children to go out and see the nearly full moon. The moon is always the same, he explains, but it reflects the light of the sun like a mirror, and each night we see a different amount of its lit side: full on the fifteenth of the month, gone on the last night, and then a new moon, which is why a month is called Chodesh, from 'something new'. Hashem gave a soft light for the night so as not to disturb our sleep. In the days of the Beis HaMikdash, witnesses reported the new moon to the Beis Din in Yerushalayim, and torches lit from mountain to mountain spread the news. After the Churban, a precise calendar was set up, and the molad is announced in shul on Shabbos Mevarchim. When Moshiach comes, the moon will shine as brightly as the sun.
display.lesson: The moon faithfully follows Hashem's command every night; looking at it should remind us how wonderful Hashem's ways are.
